Buffering/error state repainted the poster over an already revealed video
Healthy empty catalog exposed an unnecessary retry; playback retry used a play/pause toggle

changes: Controls, title/artist/required attribution and error feedback remain outside the contained video canvas; fullscreen content stays scrollable within existing safe areas
Reuse the exact shared KobraPlaybackControls used by audio; no audio design/control rewrite

Remove technical video captions/headings and unnecessary single-item carousel; retain meaningful Up next and required source credit
No new media or fallback catalog was introduced

Actual-error-only retry, duplicate retry suppression, failed recovery, late audio/Pause cancellation and disposal
One engine across metadata/fullscreen transitions; no old-session render for a changed source; stale fullscreen failure guards
Poster buffering regression and attribution-only session identity
Contain aspect ratio and controls/captions outside canvas; scrolling fullscreen; reduced motion and accessible feedback
Healthy empty/loading/catalog error distinctions; scrolling cannot select/autoplay
focusedTests.limits: Native Expo player, React Native UI, keyboard/layout and audio transport use mocks. Service/controller logic is exercised locally; this does not prove physical Android visuals, actual native video decoding, blur, orientation performance or remote streaming.

existingOriginalMedia.limits: ffprobe and ffmpeg checks validate the unchanged original local clips on Mac; they are not Android or HTTPS playback evidence. Existing clips remain in the explicit visual-review flow and do not substitute for a real catalog.

scope.existingVideoControlAndEngineMethods: UNCHANGED except friendly load-error copy; explicit retry added separately
scope.sessionIdentityChange: Attribution-only metadata updates no longer reset decoders

android.reason: No updated APK built/installed. Native video/blur/rotation/safe-area/seek/audio-handoff and device acceptance remain unverified.

remoteVideoStreaming.reason: No authorized playable remote video was verified in this stage; no URLs were invented or access controls bypassed.

restrictions: No Git commands, APK/EAS builds, backend/database/cloud changes or service restarts.
